config_name: OMEN Max 16 — Core Ultra 9 275HX, RTX 5070 Laptop 8GB, 32GB DDR5-5600, 1TB SSD, 16" WQXGA 240Hz OLED (HDR500)

specs.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX (Arrow Lake-HX, 24c/24t: 8P + 16E, up to 5.4 GHz, 156W PL2 / 109W PL1)
specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop 8GB GDDR7 (Advanced Optimus)
specs.storage_type: NVMe Gen4/Gen5 M.2 (2 slots, PCIe5 main)

offers.name: HP OMEN 16 Max 16" 240Hz HDR 500 OLED Gaming Laptop - Intel Core Ultra 9-275HX - 32GB DDR5 - 1TB SSD - RTX 5070 - Windows 11 Home - Shadow Black

reviews.quote: + high quality 240 Hz OLED panel with G-Sync
it comes with similar OLED panels as the competition and an arguably more comfortable keyboard
Its OLED panel offered vibrant colors and wide viewing angles while the speakers provided rich tin-free audio.

praises: 'The screen is magnificent and it is really nice to work or study with it' (BBY 5070 OLED owner)
'Really strong gaming laptop. I can play demanding games such as Star Citizen or MSFS 2020 in the max settings even in VR' (BBY)
OLED 240Hz with G-Sync at $3,499 CAD — the cheapest way into the panel NBC called 'high quality' in this chassis
Metal chassis, user-upgradeable RAM/SSD, anti-dust fan system (line-wide BBY praises)
BBY pool rates it 4.18/5 (n=66), the second-highest of the five CA OMEN Max tiers
complaints: 'as long as you put it in economy mode so it won't make a ridiculous loud ventilating sound' (BBY) — Unleashed mode hits ~61 dB(A) (NBC)
Glossy OLED reflects a lot: 'OLED screen is beautiful - glossy and quite a bit of reflections' (BBY)
Battery: strong only plugged in — 'Just perfect (except unplugged)' (BBY title); ~3-3.5h real-world
New NVIDIA driver regressions flagged by owners: 'Be careful with new drivers' (BBY)
Fingerprint-prone finish: 'the plastic keeps your finger tips a lot so you need to wipe it regularly' (BBY)

design_philosophy: The display-first mid tier: this is the config where buyers get the exact panel the pro-reviewed flagship shipped with (2560x1600 240Hz OLED, the class NBC scored 84% and praised as 'high quality... with G-Sync') for $1,500 less by stepping the GPU down to the RTX 5070. Same Arrow Lake-HX CPU, RAM/SSD access and chassis, so productivity and maintainability match the halo tier.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the NBC/Tom's reviewed 5090/275HX OLED config (see SHARED-omen-max16.md) — this CA tier keeps the reviewed OLED panel and CPU, only the GPU steps down: 5090→5070 = gaming −3.0 (two tiers at −1.5), ai_ml −2.0 (24→8GB VRAM), battery +0.5. screen_quality 9.0 = the anchor OLED itself (NBC Display 84%; −1 for no HDR1000 + 960Hz PWM); readability_dark 7.5 (OLED blacks, glossy reflections + PWM penalty); readability_bright 6.5 (391 nits SDR, glossy). thermals_noise 5.0: 275HX heat persists but 5070 adds less GPU heat than anchor.
